## Bottom line
**Suggests Normal (82%)** · Unreliable input · Careful review
Input is flagged and Benign stays in the conformal set; invasive probability is under 1% [F1].

## Confidence
| Signal | Value | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| Top probabilities | Normal 82%, Benign 18% | Normal leads, Benign plausible |
| Conformal set | Normal, Benign (90%) | Cannot separate the two |
| Reliability / OOD | 0.28 / 32nd percentile | Flagged; input suspect |
| Second-model (MUSK) agreement | No | Models disagree on top class |
| Similar cases | 4 of 5 Normal | Supports Normal |

## Tissue evidence
- **Normal lobules** (regions 7, 9, 10) · ↓ invasive · Strongest lower-invasive association; spot check 0/20 [F2] · Unreliable
- **Lymphocytic infiltrate (TILs)** (regions 0, 3, 4) · context · Descriptive only; spot check 8/20 [F3] · Weak
- **Benign stroma or fat** (regions 0, 7, 10) · ↓ invasive · Lower-invasive association; spot check 20/20 [F4] · Validated
- **Neoplastic nuclei** (regions 8, 10, 11) · context · Only 1 counted; cell features not computed · Measured

## Trust check
- **Heatmap**: Deletion CI excludes 0 (+0.54 logit, 0.47–0.60); faithful to the classifier.
- **Concepts**: Deletion CI includes 0 (+0.002, −0.005–0.007); not shown to reflect the classifier. Normal lobules is Unreliable.

## Could be wrong if
- Image quality is poor (reliability 0.28), so these probabilities may not hold.
- The true class is Benign; the MUSK model picks a different top class.

## Check on the slide
1. **Regions 7, 9, 10** — confirm normal lobules with two-layered epithelium; this concept failed its spot check.
2. **Regions 0, 3, 4** — check whether the lymphocytic infiltrate is real; spot check was only 8/20.
3. **Regions 8, 10, 11** — only these were segmented; one neoplastic nucleus found, so scan other regions.
